rfi.title: West Bank village siege fuels concern over growing settler violence
rfi.description: Palestinian families remained trapped in their homes in the occupied West Bank village of Qusra for an 11th day on Thursday, in a case that has drawn condemnation from US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee and become a symbol of growing settler violence in the territory.

rfi.title: Spain to open shelters in Ceuta for migrants and transfer 500 girls to mainland
rfi.description: Spain will open temporary shelters for up to 1,800 migrants in Ceuta, its enclave in Morocco, as authorities tackle the humanitarian crisis resulting from tens of thousands of people attempting to enter the territory last month. The government is also preparing to transfer 500 unaccompanied migrant girls to mainland Spain, despite opposition from Ceuta authorities.

rfi.title: US-backed Gaza peace plan ‘fails to overcome central obstacles’, warns expert
rfi.description: Talks aimed at ending the war between Israel and Gaza hit an impasse this week, with the United States playing mediator between the two parties. Amjad Iraqi, a senior Israel-Palestine analyst with the International Crisis Group, tells RFI there remain major issues that the US-backed roadmap to peace does not address.

rfi.title: French hospital helicopter landings disrupted by illegal prison delivery drones
rfi.description: Emergency helicopter landings at Strasbourg University Hospitals have been suspended over the risk of collision with drones used to illegally deliver items to inmates in a nearby prison. The hospital says the resulting detour could be "life-threatening" for patients.

rfi.title: Five years on from first vaccine, fight against malaria sees progress in Africa
rfi.description: On World Mosquito Day, attention remains focused on the devastating impact of the disease in Africa. The continent accounts for 95 per cent of malaria-related deaths worldwide. Five years after the roll-out of the first malaria vaccine, it is beginning to deliver measurable results – although significant challenges remain.

rfi.title: Rights group calls for release of two French journalists held in Togo
rfi.description: Two French journalists detained in Togo since late July have been placed in pre-trial detention and charged with "false statements", Reporters Without Borders (RSF) has said, calling for their immediate release.

rfi.title: French winegrowers begin record early harvest as heat and drought bite
rfi.description: Drought and heatwaves have pushed French winegrowers to start picking grapes weeks ahead of schedule, with this year seeing some of the earliest harvests on record – a sign of how climate change is reshaping the wine calendar across the country.

rfi.title: July heatwave sees 1,243 deaths in France, bringing summer toll to 7,300
rfi.description: More than 1,200 excess deaths were recorded in France during the country's July heatwave, bringing the provisional death toll from extreme temperatures this year to 7,300.

rfi.title: Twenty years after Probo Koala, Africa still grapples with ‘waste colonialism’
rfi.description: Twenty years after toxic waste from the cargo ship Probo Koala was dumped across Abidjan in Côte d'Ivoire, the disaster remains an open wound for many victims and a symbol of wealthy countries sending unwanted waste to Africa.

rfi.title: Ukraine war was Putin's 'fatal mistake' says Russian politician exiled in Paris
rfi.description: Russian politician and prominent Kremlin critic Boris Nadezhdin was forced to flee Russia when he found himself barred from running for election and facing imprisonment. Two weeks after arriving in Paris, he spoke to RFI about the circumstances of his exile.

rfi.title: Liberia to take in up to 1,200 US deportees within a year
rfi.description: Liberia has announced it will receive up to 1,200 foreign nationals deported from the United States – one of the largest known deals struck with African countries as part of President Donald Trump's unprecedented bid to drive out undocumented migrants.

rfi.title: Nigeria election campaign begins as voters grapple with inflation crisis
rfi.description: Campaigning kicks off in Nigeria Wednesday, five months ahead of elections set to be dominated by crushing inflation and President Bola Tinubu's economic reforms.

rfi.title: France's pioneering women's rights minister Yvette Roudy dies aged 97
rfi.description: Yvette Roudy, France's first women's rights minister and a leading figure in the country's feminist movement, has died at the age of 97.

rfi.title: Angélique Kidjo says Hollywood star is 'for Africa, but also for France'
rfi.description: Singer Angélique Kidjo has become the first black African performer to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame – telling RFI the honour represented “a door opening” at a time of global turmoil.

rfi.title: France to expel two Iranian diplomats amid growing 'interference' row
rfi.description: France will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days in response to Iran's decision to bar two French embassy staff from returning to Tehran, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot has said.

rfi.title: Southwest France steps up mosquito control after 20 chikungunya cases
rfi.description: Mosquito control operations are being stepped up across southwestern France after more than 20 locally contracted cases of the chikungunya virus were recorded since the beginning of August, with infections reported in three departments.

rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot on Tuesday became the first French woman to perform a spacewalk, carrying out a mission to repair a communications system on the International Space Station (ISS).

france24fr.title: Le président libanais reçu par le pape Léon XIV
france24fr.description:
🇱🇧🇻🇦 Le pape Léon XIV a accueilli Joseph Aoun, ce jeudi 20 août au Vatican, lors d'une audience privée. 
 
➡️ Une rencontre lors de laquelle a été évoquée la situation dans le sud du Liban, alors  qu'Israël continue de mener des frappes dans le pays.

france24fr.title: Harry et Meghan : le retour surprise au Royaume-Uni après six ans
france24fr.description: Six ans après leur départ pour les États-Unis et leur retrait de la vie royale, le prince Harry et Meghan Markle s’apprêtent à revenir vivre au Royaume-Uni avec leurs deux enfants. Explications de Philip Turtle, chroniqueur France 24.

france24fr.title: Basketball : Victor Wembanyama capitaine pour son retour en équipe de France
france24fr.description: 🏀 Victor #Wembanyama fait son grand retour avec les Bleus : nommé capitaine, le joueur des San Antonio Spurs retrouve l’équipe de France de #basket deux ans après la finale olympique de 2024, pour préparer les qualifications au Mondial 2027.

france24fr.title: Ceuta : de nouveaux centres d’accueil, Madrid toujours dans l’impasse
france24fr.description: Face à la saturation des structures d’accueil, l’Espagne a ouvert deux centres temporaires à Ceuta pour héberger les migrants qui dormaient dans la rue ou sur les plages. Deux autres sites doivent progressivement ouvrir, pour atteindre jusqu’à 4 000 places. Correspondance de Victoria David depuis Madrid pour France 24.

france24fr.title: À la frontière de Ceuta, des familles marocaines à la recherche de leurs enfants disparus
france24fr.description: Des familles marocaines sont à la recherche de leurs proches, partis fin juillet pour l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta, lors d'une importante vague migratoire. Nombre d’entre elles campent devant le poste-frontière de Tarajal, côté marocain, dans l’espoir d’obtenir des informations. L'Espagne a donc ouvert un bureau spécial pour les personnes disparues.

france24fr.title: Gaza : une crise humanitaire qui prive les civils de tout
france24fr.description: À Gaza, la crise humanitaire reste dramatique. La grande majorité de la population est toujours déplacée et vit dans des abris précaires, tandis que l’accès à l’eau potable, à la nourriture et aux logements demeure extrêmement limité. Pour en parler, France 24 reçoit Olivier Routeau, directeur des opérations pour Première Urgence Internationale.

france24fr.title: L'étoile la plus rapide de notre galaxie file à une vitesse de 25 000 kilomètres par seconde
france24fr.description: Des astronomes ont découvert l'étoile la plus rapide de la Voie lactée, baptisée S301. Elle orbite à la vitesse vertigineuse de 25 000 kilomètres par seconde autour du trou noir supermassif au centre de notre galaxie.

france24fr.title: Angélique Kidjo, première artiste africaine étoilée à Hollywood
france24fr.description: La chanteuse franco-béninoise Angélique Kidjo est devenue la première artiste africaine à recevoir une étoile sur le Hollywood Walk of Fame. À Los Angeles, plusieurs figures du cinéma et de la musique ont célébré cette consécration historique. Récit de Clarisse Fortuné.

france24fr.title: Libye : des politiques de l'Ouest et du Sud réunis à Tunis
france24fr.description: En Libye, les coupures d'électricité et l'inflation alimentent les tensions dans l'Ouest du pays, où le gouvernement d'Abdel Hamid Dbeibah est de plus en plus contesté. À Tunis, plusieurs responsables politiques de l'Ouest et du Sud libyens tentent de trouver une issue à la crise politique. Correspondance de Lilia Blaise.

france24fr.title: Guinée : l'activiste Bella Bah condamné pour injures et diffamation
france24fr.description: En Guinée, l'activiste Bella Bah a été condamné à six mois de prison, dont cinq avec sursis, pour injures et diffamation envers le grand imam de Conakry. Ancien membre du Front national pour la défense de la Constitution, il est connu pour ses prises de position critiques envers le pouvoir. Correspondance de Malick Diakité.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : la dette publique franchit le seuil historique des 40 000 milliards
france24fr.description: La dette publique américaine a dépassé pour la première fois les 40 000 milliards de dollars, selon les données du Trésor américain. Un niveau record, expliqué par Marc Paupe.

france24fr.title: Corée du Nord : une dizaine de missiles tirés vers la mer du Japon
france24fr.description: La Corée du Nord a tiré environ dix missiles balistiques de courte portée depuis la région de Pyongyang, en direction de la mer du Japon. Ces lancements interviennent alors que les exercices militaires conjoints entre les États-Unis et la Corée du Sud touchent à leur fin. Explications de Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international.

france24fr.title: Bangladesh : les bus roses arrivent à Dacca
france24fr.description: À Dacca, des bus roses réservés aux femmes prennent la route. Une réponse aux difficultés rencontrées dans les transports publics, mais aussi un symbole : au volant comme dans le bus, les femmes veulent désormais prendre leur place.

france24fr.title: Togo : l'inquiétude des familles des deux réalisateurs français détenus
france24fr.description: Reporters sans frontières a appelé, mercredi, à la "libération immédiate" des deux réalisateurs français qui ont été arrêtés le 27 juillet au Togo, où ils sont détenus avec un collaborateur local. Les familles ont fait part de leur inquiétude, "notamment pour leur santé".

france24fr.title: France : le gouvernement créé une "nouvelle unité cyber"
france24fr.description: Après plusieurs cyberattaques visant des administrations françaises, le gouvernement veut accélérer sa riposte. Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu demande à l’ANSSI de créer, sous trois jours, une nouvelle unité cyber capable d’intervenir dès qu’un accès sensible est compromis. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Canicule en Europe : 14 000 décès liés à la chaleur en Allemagne, près de 4 500 en Espagne
france24fr.description: Environ 14 000 personnes sont mortes cet été en Allemagne à cause des épisodes de canicule, selon des estimations publiées jeudi par l'autorité sanitaire allemande. En Espagne, près de 4 500 décès attribuables à la chaleur ont été recensés en Espagne entre le 1er juin et le 19 août, selon des données de l'Institut de santé Carlos III à Madrid.

france24fr.title: Le dossier de la Syrie ravive la rivalité entre Israël et la Turquie
france24fr.description: Le bombardement par Israël d’un aéroport militaire dans le nord-ouest de la Syrie, juste après la visite d'une délégation officielle turque, a provoqué une vive crispation entre les deux pays. Israël juge sa sécurité menacée et reproche à la Turquie de mener de "dangereuses aventures" dans le pays voisin.

nzz.title: Andri Silberschmidt erhält den Bonny-Preis
nzz.description: Hohe Ehre für den Zürcher FDP-Nationalrat. Der Politiker erhält den mit 100 000 Franken dotierten Freiheitspreis. Die liberale Bonny-Stiftung würdigt den 32-Jährigen für seinen Einsatz für Generationengerechtigkeit und bessere Rahmenbedingungen für Unternehmen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Roche baut Produktion in den USA weiter aus
Schweiz und China schliessen Verhandlungen über Optimierung des Freihandelsabkommens ab
nzz.description: Die Schweiz und China haben sich überraschend schnell auf eine Modernisierung ihres Freihandelsabkommens geeinigt. Diese soll Schweizer Exporteuren wesentliche Vorteile und Erleichterungen gegenüber der europäischen Konkurrenz sichern.

nzz.title: Die Schuldenlast der USA drückt massiv, das Finanzministerium interveniert am Markt für Staatsanleihen. «Es droht ein Vertrauensverlust», sagt ein Anlageexperte
nzz.description: Das amerikanische Finanzministerium will den Renditeanstieg bei Staatsanleihen mit höheren Rückkäufen bremsen. An den Kernproblemen der USA – zu hohe Ausgaben und zu hohe Schulden – ändert dies aber nichts.

nzz.title: Bundesrat entscheidet bis Ende Jahr über ein zweites Luftabwehrsystem grösserer Reichweite
nzz.description: Das VBS hat seine Grossprojekte analysiert und sieht einen «leicht positiven Trend». Einzig die bodengestützte Luftverteidigung ist nicht auf Kurs.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Wohliger Grusel: Die Androhung von Zwangsmassnahmen gegen eine AfD-Regierung ist beste Wahlwerbung für die Partei
nzz.description: Seit Tagen spekulieren Amtsträger darüber, wie man eine von der Partei geführte Landesregierung disziplinieren könnte. Hat man in Deutschland wirklich so wenig aus der Wahl von Donald Trump gelernt?

nzz.title: Nordkorea antwortet auf Trumps Annäherungsversuche mit Raketentests – wie viele Atomwaffen hat das Land?
nzz.description: Pjongjang macht klar, dass es nichts wissen will von einem Dialog mit Washington.

nzz.title: Giftalarm in Zürich: Dutzende von Einsatzkräften rücken unter Blaulicht ins Seefeld aus
nzz.description: In einem Bürogebäude ist am Donnerstag eine verdächtige Substanz entdeckt worden. Später kann Schutz und Rettung Entwarnung geben.

nzz.title: Finanzierung der 13. AHV-Rente: Die Gewerkschaften wollen wieder Kampagne machen
nzz.description: Eigentlich wollten sie den Sozialausbau mit höheren Lohnbeiträgen bezahlen, jetzt müssen die Gewerkschaften die Bevölkerung von einer Steuererhöhung überzeugen.

nzz.title: Der SRG-Präsident Jean-Michel Cina tritt ab, der logische Nachfolger sagt ab – bleibt die SRG eine Bastion der alten CVP?
nzz.description: Der Mitte-Nationalrat Gerhard Pfister sagt: Es wäre eine Belastung für die Partei. Die SRG solle entpolitisiert werden.

nzz.title: Shannon Miller wurde wegen ihrer sexuellen Orientierung entlassen, erhielt eine Abfindung von 4,5 Millionen Dollar – und ist jetzt Schweizer Nationaltrainerin
nzz.description: Die Kanadierin war die erfolgreichste Trainerin im amerikanischen College-Eishockey und klagte erfolgreich gegen ihre Absetzung. Mit 62 ist sie Schweizer Nationaltrainerin geworden, nach sieben Jahren ohne Trainerposten. Kann das gutgehen?

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Rechnung für die US-Staatsverschuldung wird beängstigend hoch. Das dominiert zusehends die Politik
nzz.description: Es gibt keinen «free lunch»; man kann mit Schulden die Kosten nur hinauszögern. Überbordet die Schuldenwirtschaft, schadet das am Schluss immer den Sparern.

nzz.title: Das Fernziel Krebsimpfung rückt näher
nzz.description: Vielversprechende Daten der Pharmafirmen Moderna und Merck lassen Patienten und Investoren hoffen. Für eine breite Anwendung der Technologie gibt es allerdings noch Hürden.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Karikatur der Woche
nzz.description: Der Karikaturist Peter Gut kommentiert in seinen wöchentlichen Zeichnungen für die NZZ das Weltgeschehen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Waadtländer Staatsanwaltschaft stellt Verfahren wegen Verletzung des Amtsgeheimnisses in der Causa Dittli ein

nzz.description: Wanda Traczyk-Stawska war Kämpferin, unermüdliche Hüterin der Erinnerung, eine moralische Autorität in Polen. Sie wurde 99 Jahre alt.

zeit.description: Bei einer AfD-Veranstaltung hatte der Kabarettist Uwe Steimle indirekt zu Gewalt gegen den Bundeskanzler aufgerufen. Wiederholt er das, droht ihm eine Vertragsstrafe.

observador.title: Harvard paga 45 milhões após venda de corpos doados
observador.description: Antigo gestor do programa de doações anatómicas foi condenado a oito anos de prisão por vender restos mortais online. Desmembrava cadáveres e enviava-os por correio aos compradores.

observador.title: "Karma". Irmã de Jong-un elogia decisão dos EUA sobre Seul
observador.description: Kim Yo-jong sublinha boa relação do irmão com Trump, mas admitiu não saber da existência de contactos recentes entre os dois. Acusa Seul de fazer "jogos de guerra" e do anúncio ter terminado com tal.

observador.title: Autarca proíbe bicicletas em Como após ter sido atropelado
observador.description: A medida abrange 30 ruas e entra em vigor em setembro. Críticos acusam o autarca de "transformar problemas individuais em problemas coletivos".

observador.title: Novo porta-aviões dos EUA chega ao Médio Oriente
observador.description: Destacado desde novembro de 2025 e com a missão estendida pelo conflito com o Irão, o Abraham Lincoln será substituído pelo George Washington, já a operar no mar Arábico desde quarta-feira.

observador.title: Tusk diz que fronteira polaca está "mais segura"
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro polaco afirmou que o projeto de defesa do país, avaliado em 2,3 mil milhões de euros, está em constante modernização. Donald Tusk destacou ainda o "Escudo Oriental".

observador.title: Viseu. Residentes com transportes públicos gratuitos
observador.description: O regime vai afetar todos os residentes com idade igual ou superior a 24 anos. Os passes podem ser pedidos a partir de segunda-feira e a medida entra em vigor a 1 de setembro.

observador.title: Trotinetas elétricas em Lisboa: sim ou não?
observador.description: Rosário Abreu Lima, diretora de comunicação institucional do ACP, confirma a proposta de um referendo municipal sobre a presença de trotinetas em Lisboa. Alerta ainda para os perigos destes veículos.

observador.title: 18h. IPMA. Esperada chuva e vento forte nos próximos dias
observador.description: IPMA avisa para a chegada de uma depressão a Portugal Continental, pouco habitual na altura do verão. Ainda, Governo garante que não tenciona avançar para uma reforma estrutural da Segurança Social.

observador.title: Unicef precisa de 150 mil dólares para mpox na Guiné-Bissau
observador.description: Sete casos confirmados e 46 suspeitos, 23 dos quais em crianças. A Unicef pede 150 mil dólares de emergência e alerta para riscos com o regresso às aulas.

observador.title: Guarda Revolucionária ameaça usar mísseis mais poderosos
observador.description: Porta-voz da Guarda Revolucionária diz que "qualquer possibilidade é concebível". Negociador iraniano recusa abrir Ormuz enquanto Washington não cumprir compromissos de junho.

observador.title: Inês Lourenço homenageada na Feira do Livro do Porto
observador.description: A poeta de 83 anos recebe uma Tília de Homenagem na Feira do Livro do Porto, que abre esta sexta-feira com mais de 200 iniciativas nos Jardins do Palácio de Cristal.

observador.title: Comunidade ucraniana celebra 35 anos de independência
observador.description: "Celebramos com orgulho, mas também com lágrimas", diz organização. Evento decorre segunda-feira e inclui leilão para apoiar crianças que estudam em abrigos na Ucrânia.

observador.title: UNITA faz queixa-crime contra polícia angolana e governador
observador.description: A queixa-crime apresentada pelo maior partido da oposição angolana refere o alegado ataque a militantes. A UNITA menciona fortes indícios de premeditação e vê o comportamento da polícia como parcial.

observador.title: Harry, Meghan e a operação "Degelo" que aqueceu o verão real
observador.description: Acompanhamos os novos capítulos do verão quente da realeza que promete estender-se para lá de setembro, e ainda recuperamos as imagens e bastidores do casamento de Cristiano e Georgina.

observador.title: Televisão pública húngara regressa após 44 dias de suspensão
observador.description: A reforma dos média públicos era um dos "principais compromissos" da campanha de Péter Magyar. A primeira emissão começou com uma reportagem sobre András Baka, o novo chefe de Estado.

observador.title: Participação "relevante" na REN justifica prémio ao vendedor
observador.description: Leitão Amaro explica que o preço a pagar pela segunda maior participação acionista na REN incorpora um prémio face à cotação porque se trata de uma posição "relevante" comprada de uma só vez.

observador.title: 17h. Governo volta a afastar reforma da Segurança Social
observador.description: Ministro da Presidência reitera que assunto está fechado. Ainda, Associação Nacional dos Técnicos de Emergência Médica critica relatório do INEM por não mostrar impacto das falhas na vida dos utentes.

Face à l’accélération du réchauffement climatique, l’artiste romande a invité le public mercredi soir à «se rassembler pour prendre soin du vivant». Dans «Transgresser», proposition participative et souvent drôle, l’action directe contre le capitalisme a aussi été abordée

Condamné pour diffamation après une interpellation sur l’aéroport de la Blécherette, Valéry Beaud est acquitté par le Tribunal fédéral. L’arrêt défend la liberté d’expression des élus communaux dans les débats d’intérêt général

spiegel.title: Jugend-Droge: Wie gefährlich das synthetische »Baller-Liquid« ist - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Sie haben knallige Farben und riechen nach Obst: Sogenannte »Baller-Liquids« gelten unter Minderjährigen als Trend-Droge. Was dahintersteckt – und wie Ermittler gegen skrupellose Dealer vorgehen.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz im Urlaub: Ein Kanzler, der gar nichts sagt, sagt auch nichts Dummes
spiegel.description: Der Bundeskanzler verlängert seine Ferien und wird direkt kritisiert: Wollte Friedrich Merz nicht eben noch, dass alle mehr arbeiten? Ach was, es geht ihm schließlich um mehr. Viel mehr.

spiegel.title: Israel – Westjordanland: Deutschland, Frankreich, Großbritannien und Italien verurteilen »E1«-Pläne
spiegel.description: Mit dem »E1«-Plan will Israel auf palästinensischem Gebiet neue Siedlungen bauen. Jetzt reagieren Berlin, Paris, London und Rom auf entsprechende Ausschreibungen. Sie drohen auch Bauunternehmern.

spiegel.title: AfD und der Fall Arno Bausemer: Gewalt ist in der AfD jetzt salonfähig
spiegel.description: Ein AfD-Abgeordneter geht mit einem Baseballschläger auf einen 14-Jährigen los, die Partei distanziert sich nicht. Immer mehr Fälle zeigen, dass die AfD mit Gewalt gegen Gegner kein Problem hat. Manche Täter stellt sie sogar ein.

spiegel.title: Kabarettist Uwe Steimle unterschreibt Unterlassung nach Stauffenberg-Aussage
spiegel.description: Bei einer AfD-Veranstaltung hat Uwe Steimle mit verbalen Ausfällen gegen Angela Merkel und Friedrich Merz auf sich aufmerksam gemacht. Die Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt, nun hat der Kabarettist vermeintlich zurückgezogen.

spiegel.title: New York: ICE nimmt Fahrer von gekentertem Boot fest
spiegel.description: Eine Frau und ein Baby starben: Der Mann, der ein verunglücktes Boot in New York steuerte, soll abgeschoben werden. Er war nach Angaben der Regierung illegal in die USA eingereist – vor fast zwanzig Jahren.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump und das Weiße Haus: Neuer Landeplatz für Hubschrauber vorgesehen
spiegel.description: Die schnöde Wiese reicht nicht – ein neuer Hubschrauberlandeplatz muss her, befand der US-Präsident. Egal, wie schlecht die Umfragewerte, wie desaströs die Außenpolitik: Bauen geht immer. Die Frage ist nur: Wie lange hält das?

spiegel.title: Wasserknappheit: Wenn der eigene Rasen vertrocknet und der des Nachbarn grünt
spiegel.description: Es gibt Schlimmeres als einen vertrockneten Rasen. Einen vertrockneten Rasen, während der des Nachbarn grün ist, zum Beispiel. Hat der etwa gegossen?

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Warum der CDU die Spaltung im Umgang mit der AfD droht
spiegel.description: Ein CDU-Bürgermeister spendet für die AfD und ruft zur Wahl der Rechtsextremisten auf. Nur ein Einzelfall?

spiegel.title: Hamburg – Elbphilharmonie: Mehr als 40 Menschen erkrankt
spiegel.description: Betroffene klagten über Übelkeit, Schwindel und Erbrechen: An der Hamburger Elbphilharmonie ist es zu einem Großeinsatz des Rettungsdienstes gekommen. Das Essen eines externen Caterers wird verdächtigt.

spiegel.title: Spende an AfD – CDU prüft Ausschluss von Kommunalpolitiker Bernd Prange
spiegel.description: Der CDU-Bürgermeister Bernd Prange aus Sachsen-Anhalt hat die AfD mit 10.000 Euro finanziell unterstützt und zur Wahl der Partei aufgerufen. Die CDU kritisiert das Verhalten – und droht mit dem Parteiausschluss.

spiegel.title: Belgien: Waldbrand laut Behörden weitgehend unter Kontrolle
spiegel.description: Hoffnung im Hohen Venn: Im westlichen Teil des Brandgebiets ist das Feuer gebändigt. Auch für das Grenzgebiet zu Deutschland geben sich die Behörden optimistisch.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Nazi-Kartei, Steuerbetrug mit Cum-Ex-Deals, Frauke Brosius-Gersdorf
spiegel.description: Die USA verweigerten jahrelang die Rückgabe der NSDAP-Kartei. Vier Cum-Ex-Beschuldigte müssen vor Gericht. Und Frauke Brosius-Gersdorf rechnet ab. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: ADAC: Unter 20.000 Euro bekommen Sie in Deutschland kaum noch einen Neuwagen
spiegel.description: In Deutschland ist kein deutscher Neuwagen für weniger als 20.000 Euro mehr erhältlich – und andere Hersteller bieten nur wenige Modelle unter dieser Preisschwelle. Eine gute Nachricht gibt es für Fans des E-Antriebs.

spiegel.title: »How I Met Your Mother«: Josh Radnor und Kollegen sind keine Freunde fürs Leben
spiegel.description: Neun Staffeln lang drehten Josh Radnor und seine Kollegen »How I Met Your Mother«. Obwohl sie jahrelang so viel Zeit miteinander verbrachten: Heutzutage gibt es zwischen den Co-Stars kaum noch Verbindungen, sagt Radnor nun.

spiegel.title: Schlafdruck: Studie an Mäusen zeigt, wie das Gehirn Müdigkeit steuert
spiegel.description: Schlaf ist für Menschen unverzichtbar. Dennoch ist weitgehend unklar, wie das Gehirn den Schlafdruck steuert. Forschenden ist es nun aber gelungen, die Mechanismen besser zu verstehen.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Hackerangriff bedroht Tausende Wohngeldzahlungen
spiegel.description: Fast eine Woche nach einer Cyberattacke sind Teile der Berliner Verwaltung noch nicht wieder arbeitsfähig. Für manche Berlinerinnen und Berliner hat das spürbare Folgen.

spiegel.title: Rumänischer Kampfjet zerstört offenbar Seedrohne nahe Gasplattform im Schwarzen Meer
spiegel.description: Nach Angaben des rumänischen Verteidigungsministeriums wurde eine nicht identifizierte Drohne auf dem Meer nahe der Grenze zur Ukraine abgeschossen. Rumäniens Präsident macht Russland verantwortlich.

nyt.title: Treasury Turns to Interventionist Tactics to Lower Interest Rates
nyt.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is reinventing the government’s role in the world’s most important bond market.

nyt.title: Bond Market Stress Returns and Oil Rises in Edgy Day for Markets
nyt.description: Bond markets remained volatile, as investors assessed the geopolitical turmoil.

nyt.title: Walmart Posts Slowest Sales Growth in Years as Americans Tighten Wallets
nyt.description: Walmart and other big U.S. retailers have warned that consumers were being cautious, even if household balance sheets seemed healthy.

nyt.title: Canada and U.S. Resume Talks Over Trump Tariffs as a New Deadline Looms
nyt.description: While President Trump has declared that the two countries effectively have a deal, they remain apart on several key issues.

nyt.title: As Iran and U.S. Settle Into an Uneasy Standoff, Who Will Blink First?
nyt.description: For weeks, there has been no diplomatic progress, but also no full-scale fighting, as each side seems to believe it can hold out longer than the other.

nyt.title: Trump’s Economic Threat Puts Focus on Iran’s Trading Partners
nyt.description: President Trump appeared to suggest that the United States would impose economic penalties on countries that do business with Iran, though he did not specify what actions he would take.

nyt.title: How Trump Is Trying to Crush California’s Climate Policies
nyt.description: At least a half-dozen federal agencies have taken action against the state that has led the nation in environmental protections.

nyt.title: After Six Years, Harry and Meghan Are Coming Home. What Changed?
nyt.description: Just last year, Prince Harry said he couldn’t imagine ever bringing his family back to Britain.

nyt.title: What to Know About Prince Harry and Meghan’s Move Back to the U.K.
nyt.description: The couple are moving back after six years in the United States. What they will do, and much else, are still unclear.

nyt.title: As Prince Harry and Meghan Depart California for the U.K., Their Neighbors Shrug
nyt.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle self exiled to the ultrawealthy enclave of Montecito in 2020. “They wave. They drive. They close the gates,” a neighbor said.

nyt.title: Can We Do Anything About Tick-Borne Diseases Like Alpha-Gal Syndrome?
nyt.description: A scientific and civilizational horror story.

nyt.title: Trump’s Order to Cut Military Exercises With South Korea Carries Risks, Experts Say
nyt.description: President Trump’s decision to curtail the military exercises came as allies question the U.S. commitment to longstanding alliances.

nyt.title: First U.S. Deportees to Arrive in Liberia Amid Growing Backlash
nyt.description: Critics in the small West African nation say their government has not said why it agreed to one of the largest U.S. deportation deals, who the deportees are, or how they will be handled.

nyt.title: State Dept. Declares U.S. Citizen in China Wrongfully Detained
nyt.description: U Min Zin, a scholar who studied Myanmar, is one of two U.S. citizens the department has designated as wrongfully detained in China.

nyt.title: Under Trump, Protected Wild Horses Are Going to Slaughter
nyt.description: A legal loophole allows the government to sell mustangs on the cheap, stripping them of protections and clearing their path to destruction.

nyt.title: Ken Paxton’s $1,000 Pen Incident Resurfaces in Texas Senate Race
nyt.description: The pen Mr. Paxton pocketed more than a decade ago has resurfaced as a campaign issue.

nyt.title: ‘The Necessary Conversation’ Puts Family Political Arguments On Full Display
nyt.description: “The Necessary Conversation,” a podcast and YouTube show, is a very public example of the political disputes families are having all across the country.

nyt.title: FBI Agents Search Eric Swalwell’s Home as Part of Federal Sexual Assault Inquiry
nyt.description: Most sex crimes are prosecuted by state and local authorities. The federal agents appeared to be using civil rights statutes to scrutinize Mr. Swalwell’s conduct, a person familiar with the case said.

npr.title: U.S. debt tops $40 trillion. And, new census report Trump is touting raises concerns
npr.description: The U.S. debt has surpassed $40 trillion. And, a new census report on noncitizen voting that President Trump is touting has ties to a think tank aligned with him, raising concerns among experts.

npr.title: North Korea fires a suspected missile toward the sea, Japan says
npr.description: The suspected launch on Thursday comes a day after North Korea shrugged off a U.S. decision to scale back military drills with South Korea in an apparent bid to resume diplomacy.

npr.title: Chinese court sentences founder of property developer Evergrande to life in prison
npr.description: Chinese property developer Hui Ka Yan has been sentenced to life in prison. The decision marks a milestone in Evergrande's saga after it collapsed with more than $300 billion in liabilities.

npr.title: Prince Harry and Meghan are returning to the U.K. with their children
npr.description: Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, have decided to return to the United Kingdom for an extended stay starting this fall, but they won't resume their roles as working members of the royal family.

npr.title: Israeli military launches criminal probes into killings of 5-year-old and paramedics
npr.description: Israel's military on Wednesday announced its first criminal investigations into troop conduct in Gaza, focusing on the killings of 5-year-old Hind Rajab and her family and of 15 Palestinian paramedics.

npr.title: More than 1,000 Afghan refugees have been stuck at a camp in Qatar since 2021
npr.description: More than 1,000 Afghan refugees who fled their homes in 2021 have been stuck in Camp As-Sayliyah, Qatar. They're isolated and unable to leave, despite many having aided U.S. forces during the war.

npr.title: Amid the Iran war, the U.S. has pivoted it's geopolitical attention away from Asia
npr.description: A decade ago, the U.S. was still in its "pivot to Asia." Today, as conflicts in the Middle East suck up American military resources, analysts say that pivot is over — or never really began.

npr.title: Israel launches probe into killing of 5-year-old girl and medics sent to rescue her
npr.description: Israel is launching a criminal investigation into the Gaza killings carried out by Israeli troops of a 5-year-old girl and her family and the medics sent to rescue her.

npr.title: Why does the U.S. military seem stymied in the war with Iran?
npr.description: Defense analyst Stacie Pettyjohn says while the U.S. military is facing long-range missile shortages, prolonged deployments and vacated regional bases, Iran is building cheaper weapons quickly.

npr.title: Greetings from Trouville-sur-Mer, a beach town little changed since Monet painted it
npr.description: The Normandy beach town of Trouville-sur-Mer is a two-hour train ride from Paris, but feels a world away, with English Channel breezes and the sound of seagulls screeching through the cobbled streets.

republika.description: Per la prima volta una delle specie più amate (e dipinte) dal pittore non ha resistito all’estate, mentre i fiori d’acqua non hanno subito danni. Ora i giardinieri pensano al futuro

republika.description: È partita la Carovana dei Ghiacciai di Legambiente. Dal 2000 la loro superficie sulle Alpi si è ridotta del 39 per cento. Claudio Smiraglia, glaciologo: “Sono 65 anni che studio il Forni e mai l’avevo visto così scuro e spezzettato”

republika.description: Il ritrovamento sulle montagne svizzere, al confine con l’Italia. Uno scalatore ha notato i due corpi e ha dato l’allarme. Sull’Everest sono stati recuperati i cadaveri di Marco Di Marcello e Markus Kirchler, uccisi da una valanga a novembre

republika.description: Dalle escursioni affrontate senza preparazione alle richieste immotivate in mare: dal 2026 chi provoca un intervento per dolo o colpa grave può essere chiamato a pagare personale, mezzi ed elicotteri. Ma un errore non basta e chiedere aiuto quando esiste un pericolo resta sempre la scelta giusta

republika.description: Nato poverissimo, l’immobiliarista Hui Ka Yan è arrivato ad esser l’uomo più ricco della Cina con il boom del cemento. Poi il suo castello di debiti è crollato e con le strette di Xi il gigante si è sgretolato. Ora la decisione del tribunale di Shenzhen con la condanna a vita e una multa da 2 miliardi

elpais.description: La bisnieta del canciller que unificó Alemania, icono eterno del verano español, afronta su viudedad con vitalismo y melancolía

elpais.description: Las ‘influencers’ consideradas como adalides de este movimiento reniegan del término después de haber construido negocios millonarios gracias a su contenido, en el que promueven una vida idílica como amas de casa

elpais.description: Centros de Barcelona, Madrid, Málaga y Valencia fueron escenario de este hito médico

elpais.description: La exmilitante del PSOE insiste en acusar a la Guardia Civil y al magistrado de investigarla en secreto por “los mismos hechos” que el juez Zamarriego

phys-org.title: Blocc chemistry could automate molecular discovery and democratize access to new materials
phys-org.description: A paper published in the journal Science lays out a roadmap for broadening access to the process of discovering molecular tools that can benefit society, including medicines, materials and a wide range of everyday consumer products.

phys-org.title: Accounting staff turnover may lead to future financial reporting problems
phys-org.description: Investors looking for early signs of declining financial reporting quality may want to pay attention to employee turnover in a company's accounting department, according to new research from the University at Buffalo School of Management.

phys-org.title: 100-million-year-old molecular 'bypasses' may have helped grasses dominate landscapes and agriculture
phys-org.description: 100 million years ago, long before human intervention, ancestors of grasses, including wheat, rice and maize, developed "bypasses" in chemical pathways used to create two critical compounds: lignin and starch. These more efficient pathways could explain why grass plants are so successful in nature and agriculture, according to a new paper published in Science on Aug. 20 by researchers from the University of Wisconsin–Madison and their collaborators.

phys-org.title: Newton's momentum principles could help design safer offshore facilities in extreme waves
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a novel model to accurately and efficiently predict the impact of "green water"—water washing onto the deck of an offshore facility during extreme wave conditions.

phys-org.title: Oxygen vacancies unlock fast lithium-ion transport in battery material
phys-org.description: Lithium titanate (LTO, Li4Ti5O12) is a well-established battery material that in its pristine state is a poor conductor of lithium ions. It develops high ionic conductivity only during charging, when additional lithium ions and electrons are incorporated into the material.

phys-org.title: Soil methane sink may be larger than thought, three-model analysis finds
phys-org.description: Methane-munching microbes in soil might be more important than previously thought, a new study finds. Soil is an important carbon sink, and scientists are still learning much about the diversity of its microbial communities. They're being uncovered from Arctic soils to desert sands, and some of them are sucking down methane—a greenhouse gas about 27–30 times more potent than carbon dioxide over 100 years.

phys-org.title: Temporary liver coating may improve safety and targeting of mRNA vaccines and cancer therapies
phys-org.description: With the commercialization of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19, research and development into the application of mRNA in vaccines and pharmaceuticals is accelerating. In particular, it is attracting attention not only in vaccines for preventing infectious diseases but also in cancer immunotherapy.

phys-org.title: Farm mice study shows antibiotic resistance is an environmental problem, not just a medical one
phys-org.description: Scientists analyzed the genomes of gut microorganisms from an extensive population of 875 wild house mice (Mus musculus) collected from farms in Germany. They searched for genes responsible for resistance to common antibiotics and correlated the presence of these ARGs in the mice with a range of environmental and host variables, such as land use and farming practices, livestock density for cattle, pigs and poultry, sex and physical condition of the mice, as well as climatic variables.

phys-org.title: Women compete just as hard as men for top jobs and can win them more often, auction-style study suggests
phys-org.description: New behavioral economics research on gender and competition, using bidding experiments, finds no overall gender gap in competitiveness; where a gap does appear, it is women who push hardest for the highest positions.

phys-org.title: DNA's physical properties may shape which mutations evolution preserves
phys-org.description: Nearly every cell in the human body contains essentially the same genetic information, yet different cells activate different genes. For regulatory proteins to reach these genes, DNA must be accessible. This accessibility depends not only on the genetic code itself but also on DNA's physical properties—its shape, flexibility and ability to interact with proteins.

phys-org.title: Preschool teachers overwhelmingly support play-based learning, study finds
phys-org.description: Thinkers from Plato to Maria Montessori have championed play as one of the most powerful ways that young children learn and grow. American preschool teachers overwhelmingly agree—but a new study finds that teachers in urban settings feel less family support for play-based learning than their suburban counterparts.

phys-org.title: A little Big Bang: Bowling-pin-shaped nuclei shed new light on the universe's first moments
phys-org.description: What happened in the first moments of the universe—before the building blocks of life and the world we know today came into existence? Physicists at the CERN research facility in Switzerland are trying to answer this question by recreating some of the extreme conditions that prevailed in the universe during its earliest history. phys-org.title: 3D imaging and machine learning improve noncontact weight estimation of frozen skipjack tuna
phys-org.description: Accurately determining fish body size and weight is essential for fisheries resource management and seafood processing; however, measuring large quantities of fish is labor-intensive, and results may vary among operators.

phys-org.title: Neanderthal hips challenge long-standing hypothesis of a trade-off between childbirth and bipedal walking
phys-org.description: The most prominent difference between human male and female skeletons is the pelvis, which anthropologists often use to determine the sex of ancient remains. Scientists have long believed the human pelvis evolved mainly as a compromise between walking on two legs and giving birth to large-brained babies. This idea is known as the Obstetrical Dilemma Hypothesis.

phys-org.title: International review standardizes selenosugar nomenclature and selenium metabolism
phys-org.description: Selenosugars are the major urinary metabolites responsible for the physiological excretion of selenium. Understanding selenium metabolism relies on accurately detecting and identifying selenosugars. However, research has been hindered by inconsistent terminology used for selenosugars, varying analytical practices and an incomplete understanding of the biological pathway for selenosugar biosynthesis.

phys-org.title: Illuminating the limits of the international unit of light, the candela
phys-org.description: The candela, the international unit of light in use for almost a century, forms the basis of photometry. According to a new study, measurements derived from it systematically misjudge the brightness of colored light sources and depart markedly from human perception.

phys-org.title: Nanoparticle combines two strategies to speed up the healing of chronic wounds
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) in Ribeirão Preto, Brazil, have developed a nanoparticle that can address the various factors hindering the healing of chronic wounds, which include ulcers associated with diabetes and pressure ulcers common among bedridden individuals. phys-org.description: When was the last time you bought a loaf of bread?

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
proj-syn.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead. Instead, it is to build the capacity to make surviving that loss possible, such as by investing in AI infrastructure and training capabilities.

proj-syn.title: MDBs Are Becoming a New Global Safe Asset
proj-syn.description: Even as multilateralism faces an existential threat, multilateral development banks are not only surviving but thriving. Thanks to MDBs’ ability to borrow at costs close to that of the US Treasury, they have created a new class of de facto risk-free assets that could help underpin the global financial system.

proj-syn.title: Why US Bond Markets Are Trembling
proj-syn.description: What is the apparent fragility in the US bond market telling us? Since markets tend to be less wrong than those who comment on them regularly, their signals must be taken seriously, especially when they coincide with a relative softening in US inflation figures and other high-frequency economic indicators.

proj-syn.title: Look East for Lessons in Democratic Resistance
proj-syn.description: Pro-democracy activists often turn to Eastern and Central Europe for inspiration, while Asia’s remarkable democratic breakthroughs receive far less attention. Yet the continent’s recent struggles offer valuable lessons for those seeking to resist the global advance of authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Three Ways AI Will Change the Course of Humanity
proj-syn.description: The AI debate has largely focused on productivity gains and job displacement, but its consequences will reach much further By revolutionizing how we combat disease, wage wars, and stimulate income growth, AI could fundamentally alter the terms of human existence.

proj-syn.title: Global Economic Convergence Is Stalling
proj-syn.description: For a while, the world’s advanced economies (other than the US) were rapidly losing ground to their emerging counterparts. But the BRICS' catch-up momentum has stalled since 2016, not because the G7 has been doing better, but because everyone has been doing worse.

proj-syn.title: When a Big Energy Project Turns Bad
proj-syn.description: After hundreds of millions of dollars were invested by developing-country governments, and before a single watt of energy was transferred, the CASA-1000 infrastructure project in Central Asia has effectively failed. The international institutions that conceived, financed, and promoted the project must answer for this.

proj-syn.title: The Trolling of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: Democracy is most vulnerable when voters can no longer distinguish genuine abuses of power from partisan attacks. Authoritarian leaders exploit that uncertainty by blurring the line between misconduct and political theater, making legitimate criticism look like just another witch hunt.

proj-syn.title: A Future With Chinese Characteristics
proj-syn.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American, and even American young people.

proj-syn.title: Putin Has Run Out of Moves
proj-syn.description: Even with the Russian economy suffering from low growth, high inflation, and relentless Ukrainian long-range drone strikes on energy infrastructure, President Vladimir Putin has thrown fiscal caution to the wind and allowed the government’s budget deficit to balloon to 2.8% of GDP. It isn’t likely to end well.

proj-syn.title: The Geopolitical Drag on AI Governance
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration’s decision to prioritize national competitiveness over multilateral frameworks has deepened the fragmentation of AI governance—and expanded the opening for China to organize its own system. But China's approach is similarly shaped primarily by its own geopolitical ambitions.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of the China Shock
proj-syn.description: As advances in generative AI continue, US policymakers should heed two lessons from the opening of trade with China. But that will require them to rethink the conventional wisdom about deindustrialization and the decline of manufacturing employment.

proj-syn.title: Guatemala’s Democratic Renewal
proj-syn.description: Guatemalan President Bernardo Arévalo’s recent selection of an honest successor to a corrupt attorney general represents a decisive victory for the country’s democracy. Arévalo succeeded not because he abandoned institutions to save democracy, but because he trusted institutions enough to work through them.

proj-syn.title: Iceland Belongs in the Eurozone
proj-syn.description: In evaluating the trade-offs of joining the European Union and giving up their own currency, Icelanders must recognize that the costs of eurozone membership are smaller than what past data suggest. If anything, being within the eurosystem would make a repeat of Iceland's post-2008 banking crisis exceedingly unlikely.

proj-syn.title: Zhu Rongji’s Legacy of Demographic Decline
proj-syn.description: Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji’s recent death elicited widespread accolades for his role in pushing the market-oriented reforms that unleashed decades of economic growth. But Zhu also oversaw two major policy shifts that have had dire implications for China’s demographic outlook.

proj-syn.title: The Global Land Agenda’s Moment of Truth
proj-syn.description: As delegates gather this week in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, for the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the UN Convention to Combat Desertification, momentum is building toward a more ambitious global response to land degradation. In fact, there are five promising signs that this time could be different.

proj-syn.title: How Trump Is Reinvigorating Democracy
